correctness.rationale: Invariance of y gives the exact marginal pushforward y_#mu=(bx)_#mu, hence E[y]=bm. Invariance of x gives aE[x^2]+(1-b)m-1=0. Vieta for the fixed-point roots converts this exactly to Var(x)=(r_+-m)(m-r_-), and endpoint variance zero forces the fixed-point atoms. The same equation is E[a(x-r_-)(x-r_+)]=0. If that polynomial vanishes on support, invertibility gives the previous x-coordinate x_-=y/b as another root, while the next first coordinate is (1-b)x+b x_-. With 0<b<1, unequal roots would produce a strict interior convex combination, impossible if support only uses the two root levels; hence support consists of the two fixed points. Therefore every other invariant measure must charge both signs. The verifier checks the exact moment algebra and the classical radical coordinates.

final_claim: For H_{a,b}(x,y)=(1-a x^2+y,bx) with a>0 and 0<b<1, every compact invariant probability measure has Var(x)=(r_+-E[x])(E[x]-r_-), y-marginal equal to the bx-marginal, and zero mean of a(x-r_-)(x-r_+); unless supported on the two fixed points it gives positive mass both inside the fixed-point vertical strip and outside it, with endpoint means attained only by the corresponding fixed-point atoms.
